title: bin(check-opencode-metered-providers): extra arguments silently ignored — a second config path is never checked, unknown flags pass

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

body:
## What

`bin/check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs` — the guard that fails CI when a metered/PAYG provider is selected without an explicit exception (#2288) — reads only `process.argv[2]` as the config path and silently ignores every later argument:

```js
// bin/check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs:348 (main)
const configPath = resolve(process.argv[2] ?? DEFAULT_CONFIG);
```

There is no unknown/extra-argument check anywhere in the script. A second config path, a misspelled flag, or a nonexistent second path all pass without a word, and the success line names only the first file — so an invocation that looks like it checked two configs (or a config plus an option) actually checked one.

## Verified this run (laptop, real script, main 4af4ee8354, md5 9f6353d950afd810272bd5ab60dcaf65)

Probe dir: `~/git/fleet/probe-metered-argv` on the laptop. Fixtures: `good.jsonc` (plan routes only) and `bad.jsonc` (`"model": "deepseek/deepseek-chat"` — a PAYG selection the guard exists to reject).

| Run | Observed |
|---|---|
| `node check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs bad.jsonc` (control) | exit 1, names the deepseek selection |
| `node check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs good.jsonc` (control) | exit 0, "guard passed" |
| `node check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs good.jsonc bad.jsonc` | **exit 0, "guard passed: …/good.jsonc" — bad.jsonc never read** |
| `node check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs good.jsonc --bogus` | **exit 0 — unknown flag silently ignored** |
| `node check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs good.jsonc nonexistent.jsonc` | **exit 0 — the second path is never even opened** |
| `node check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs bad.jsonc good.jsonc` (order control) | exit 1 — only the first argument is ever inspected |

## Why it matters

- This guard is the automated enforcement of the no-PAYG routing rule. A green run that silently skipped the config it was asked to check is worse than no run: the success line ("Metered-provider config guard passed: <path>") gives no hint that a second target was dropped.
- The CI invocation (`.github/workflows/opencode-config-guard.yml:28`) passes exactly one path today, so this is an operator/manual-run and future-workflow-expansion hazard, not a live CI bypass — the same extra-positional class as #7555 (confirm-charges-surfaced), in a different script with different argv code.
- Distinct from #6953 (the guard workflow's missing triggers) and #4694 (its entry-point check, fixed): neither touches argument handling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Any argument after the single config path (a second positional, an unknown flag, a joined `--flag=value`) fails fast with a usage error and a non-zero exit, before the config file is read.
- [ ] Zero or one positional argument keep working exactly as today: no args checks `DEFAULT_CONFIG` (`.opencode/opencode.jsonc`); one arg checks that file; the pass/fail messages and exit codes are unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests in `bin/check-opencode-metered-providers.test.mjs` (subprocess-level, since `main()` is not exported) cover: extra positional naming a failing config, an unknown flag, and the two controls (single good config passes, single bad config fails).
- [ ] The existing fixture suite still passes (`node --test bin/check-opencode-metered-providers.test.mjs`).
